summary: In Portland, OR, Quantifying & Visualizing Urban Heat in Portland through Community Depaving is a monitoring and adaptive management initiative. Remote sensing and data mapping and collaborated with Depave, a nonprofit that engages communities in converting pavement to green spaces in vulnerable neighborhoods. The case addresses extreme Heat. Available materials report frontline communities identified-Mapped neighborhoods with both high temperature exposure and social vulnerability, emphasizing areas needing urgent attention, Depaving effectiveness-Demonstrated an average reduction of ~1 °F in surface temperature across depaved sites, highlighting quantifiable cooling benefits, and Method development: Validated a replicable approach combining remote sensing and community intervention to assess and mitigate urban heat impacts.
title: Quantifying & Visualizing Urban Heat in Portland through Community Depaving
transferability: Washington cities like Seattle face similar challenges with urban heat and environmental inequities. Adopting this study’s approach mapping social vulnerability, partnering with local nonprofits, and measuring the impact of interventions can help state and local planners prioritize heat adaptation strategies. By focusing on historically marginalized neighborhoods, this model supports healthier communities and advances environmental justice within broader climate resilience efforts.
